title: Inside a black hole: the classical singularity
example_questions: What if you fell into a black hole?
What is inside a black hole?
summary: General relativity predicts that once inside the horizon, everything reaches the central singularity in a finite proper time. Tidal forces stretch infalling objects (spaghettification). For stellar mass black holes this happens before the horizon; for supermassive ones you cross the horizon unharmed. Most physicists expect quantum gravity to replace the singularity, so this is GR's prediction rather than the final word.
support_note: This is what GR predicts (Penrose's theorem); most expect quantum effects to modify the very centre.
what_happens: Distant observers see the faller slow and redden at the horizon
The faller crosses the horizon in finite time
The singularity is reached within a maximum proper time of pi G M / c^3

objections: Singularities signal the breakdown of GR
